record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
record.original_question: When neighboring nuclei with different proton and neutron numbers are interconnected through continuum reaction channels, what determines the size and internal organization of the resulting correlated domains, or clusters, of quantum states, and how do those features depend on the binding energies of the participating states?

evidence.quote: Many-body states in neighboring nuclear systems with different proton and neutron numbers become interconnected via continuum, forming correlated domains (clusters) of quantum states.
At present, little is known about the basic features of such clusters, e.g. a typical 'cluster size' and its dependence on binding properties of participating states.

When moving towards the particle drip lines, nuclei with different proton and neutron numbers become interconnected via continuum space, i.e., reaction channels, forming correlated domains of quantum states.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a collection of atomic nuclei labeled by their proton and neutron numbers $(Z,N)$, and for each nucleus let its many-body eigenstates near the particle drip lines be coupled to one another through shared decay/reaction channels in the continuum (e.g., particle emission and capture channels). Through these continuum couplings, many-body states belonging to neighboring nuclei with different $(Z,N)$ become interconnected and organize into "correlated domains" or clusters of quantum states.

Define such a cluster precisely as a maximal connected component of the graph whose vertices are the many-body states of nuclei in some specified region of the nuclear chart, with edges given by non-negligible continuum coupling matrix elements between states (e.g., couplings exceeding a fixed threshold or, equivalently, mediated by open reaction channels with sufficient overlap).

Problem. Determine:
(a) the typical "size" of such a cluster (e.g., the number of participating many-body states, or the spread in $(Z,N)$ and excitation energy of states it contains);
(b) its internal organization (the structure of the coupling graph within a cluster, including hierarchy, connectivity, and dominant channel content);
(c) the quantitative dependence of these features on the binding energies (and separation energies) of the participating states, in particular as one approaches the proton and neutron drip lines.

Provide either rigorous results, model-independent scaling laws, or characterizations within a well-defined open quantum system framework (such as a continuum shell model or Gamow shell model formulation) for the cluster size and its binding-energy dependence.
artifact.status_search_result: No publications were found that quantitatively characterize the size and internal organization of correlated, continuum-coupled clusters of many-body nuclear states across neighboring isotopes/isotones, nor their dependence on binding energies. The question, posed in the context of nuclear open quantum systems near the drip lines, appears to remain an open conceptual and computational problem; available literature treats coupled-cluster and Gamow shell model techniques but does not address this specific cluster-of-states characterization.

status_evidence.snippet: Coupled cluster ... has been successfully applied to neutron-rich and medium-mass nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Existing coupled-cluster methods address binding energies of individual nuclei, but do not address inter-nucleus correlated domains formed via continuum coupling.
